title: Best Loan Origination Systems for CDFIs and Credit Unions
summary: A 2026 comparison of loan origination systems for CDFIs and credit unions, covering workflow automation, document intelligence, SBA tooling, and why only one platform is AI-native.
body_text: Key takeaways The LOS sets the economics of every loan: it determines how many staff hours each file takes, how fast borrowers get an answer, and what your team still does by hand. A strong LOS covers the full origination process from application to decision, handles the non-standard borrowers community lenders serve, configures to your credit policy, and generates the reports funders and examiners need. Best overall for CDFIs and credit unions: Kita Intelligent LOS, the only AI-native system in this comparison, built end to end with AI agents handling the document analysis, spreading, and memo drafting. The loan origination system sits at the center of a CDFI’s operations. It is where applications arrive, documents collect, underwriting happens, and decisions get recorded, and it determines how many staff hours each loan takes and how fast borrowers get an answer. The market has also shifted. AI can now analyze borrower documents, spread financials, and draft credit memos, which changes what an LOS can take on and what to weigh when choosing one. The platforms in this comparison automate different parts of the job: some organize the whole process end to end, some perfect a single stage like intake, and some use AI to take on the analysis itself. In this guide, we compare six origination platforms serving CDFIs and credit unions in 2026: what each covers, what each automates, and which type of institution it fits. How to think about choosing an LOS When choosing an LOS, five differences matter most: Who it was built for: Generic commercial platforms assume conventional borrowers and clean paperwork. Community lending runs on thin files, non-standard businesses, and technical assistance, and a system built for it shows that in its defaults, checklists, and reporting. What it automates: Traditional LOS platforms organize the process: applications in one place, checklists, and status tracking. A new generation of AI-native systems goes further: the LOS itself analyzes any document, spreads the financials, and drafts a cited memo in minutes instead of days. How much it molds to your process: Some systems are fixed templates you adapt your process to. Others configure around your loan products, credit policy, and memo format, with the vendor handling setup. The reporting your funders require: If CDFI Fund TLR and impact reporting take a quarterly scramble today, check whether the system produces them from data it already holds. Cost at your scale: Pricing designed for commercial banks rarely fits community-lender volume. Modular pricing lets you pay for the stages you actually adopt. 01 Lenders Cooperative Best for outsourced SBA underwriting A cloud-based commercial LOS used by banks, credit unions, CDCs, and CDFIs. End-to-end commercial workflow: Digital application through documentation intake, spreading, decisioning, and closing for small business, C&I, and SBA products. Deep SBA tooling: Purpose-built support for 7(a), 504, and other government-guaranteed programs via its 2025 merger with Ventures Lending Technologies, plus loan servicing. Shared services model: Institutions can outsource underwriting, closing, and servicing to Lenders Cooperative’s own staff when volume spikes. Best for: Lenders that want a dedicated third-party underwriting and back-office team for their SBA and government-guaranteed programs, on top of an established workflow platform. 02 LoanWell Best turnkey all-in-one An end-to-end origination platform built specifically for community lenders. Full lifecycle in one tool: From custom-branded application pages through e-signed closing packages, ACH disbursement, and repayment servicing. Flexible underwriting: Use built-in auto-decisioning or bring your own Excel models; underwriting depth depends on the models you bring. CDFI reporting: The reporting layer community lenders need for funders and the CDFI Fund. Best for: Small CDFIs and loan funds that want a turnkey, ready-made system for the whole loan lifecycle. 03 Lenderfit Best borrower intake and collaboration A borrower application and document-collection platform for CDFIs and mission-driven lenders, focused on the front of the funnel. Checklist-style portal: Customizable templates and client-facing checklists walk borrowers through exactly what to submit, with milestone tracking and a full history log. Built for technical assistance: The guided journey mirrors the TA-heavy way CDFIs work with first-time borrowers. Lightweight integrations: Connects with Google Workspace and Salesforce. Best for: CDFIs whose bottleneck is incomplete applications and document chasing, and that want a better front door without replacing their back office. 04 Salesforce Best build-your-own platform Many CDFIs build custom loan origination systems on Salesforce using Financial Services Cloud and partner applications. Fully custom workflows: Loan products, stages, and approval chains are built to your exact process, with reports and dashboards on any field you track. Ecosystem depth: AppExchange add-ons cover e-signature, document generation, and borrower portals, and nonprofit pricing is available to many CDFIs. One record with your CRM: Origination lives beside outreach, technical assistance, and funder data, so the full borrower relationship stays in one place. Best for: Lenders with Salesforce expertise in-house, or budget for a partner, that want origination shaped exactly to their process. 05 nCino Best enterprise LOS for banks and credit unions A cloud banking platform built on Salesforce, used by banks and credit unions worldwide for commercial, small business, and consumer lending. Single platform across lines: Onboarding, origination, and portfolio management for commercial, SBA, small business, and consumer products in one system of record. Built-in spreading tools: Financial statement spreading and credit analysis inside the credit workflow, with AI features arriving through its Banking Advisor assistant. Enterprise integrations: Connects to core banking systems, credit bureaus, and document providers at scale. Best for: Larger credit unions and banks with the volume and budget for an enterprise implementation measured in months. 06 Kita Intelligent LOS Best overall for CDFIs and credit unions The only AI-native loan origination system in this comparison. Intelligent LOS runs origination as one AI-powered system: it pulls in every application, analyzes every document, extracts every figure, and flags what needs human review, taking each loan from borrower application to signed memo in minutes. AI Credit Officer: Runs the borrower back-and-forth on any channel, in 30+ languages. Chases missing documents, verifies details, and flags inconsistencies until the file is complete. Kita Capture: Understands any document, any format. Where traditional template-based OCR breaks on unfamiliar layouts, photographed pages, and handwriting, Capture extracts the credit signals with up to 99.3% accuracy, reconciles claims across documents, and flags fraud in seconds. AI Underwriter: Spreads the financials, understands the story behind the numbers, and drafts the memo calibrated to your policy, with every figure cited to its source. Your team edits, reviews, and signs. Configured to your lending: Deploys around your loan products, credit policy, and memo format, with Kita’s team handling the configuration and iterating as your credit box changes. Integrates with anything: Runs as the complete origination system or connects to whatever you already run, from CRMs to core banking, with REST APIs and webhooks on every loan-file event. Auditable by design: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, with a full audit log on every file, citations on every claim, and in-region data residency. Best for: CDFIs and credit unions doing small business, SBA, or microloan lending that want origination measured in minutes and hours instead of weeks, with human sign-off on every decision. Which platform is right for you? The right platform for your institution depends on what you lend, how much of the workflow you want to automate, and whether document analysis and underwriting belong inside the tool or live elsewhere in your stack. In lending, the platform that actually works is the one that clears a real, painful bottleneck rather than the one with the most features. The scorecard below lines each platform up against the capabilities that matter most for community lenders. Capability scorecard How the six platforms compare on the dimensions that separate them. Platform End-to-end origination AI document intelligence AI-powered underwriting Built for community lenders Custom-fit to your lending process Lenders Cooperative LoanWell Lenderfit Salesforce nCino Kita Intelligent LOS Full Partial Not a focus The most advanced AI-native LOS ever built Kita built Intelligent LOS around a single idea: the system handles the tedious and manual parts of the origination process while your credit team makes the final decision. Every application, document, and decision stays logged in one system of record, with portfolio insights on top. For a mission-driven lender, that changes what the team can do. When origination drops from weeks to hours and the AI handles the document work, the hours once spent assembling files go back to borrowers, relationships, and reaching more of the communities CDFIs exist to serve. See what AI-native origination changes for your team Book a demo to walk through your loan products, your current process, and where the hours go. Book a demo Frequently asked questions What makes a loan origination system "AI-native"? An AI-native LOS does the underwriting work inside the workflow: it analyzes borrower documents, extracts and verifies the figures, spreads the financials, and drafts the credit memo, with humans reviewing output instead of producing it. A traditional LOS with an AI feature typically adds a chatbot or a document upload portal while the document review, spreading, and writing stay manual. The test is simple: after the borrower submits, does the system produce a decision-ready file or a to-do list? Can we keep our existing LOS and still get AI underwriting? Yes. Kita’s modules embed individually into an existing LOS, CRM, or core through native APIs, so you can run Capture or the AI Underwriter inside your current stack. The trade-off of any bolt-on approach is a fragmented loan file: intake, analysis, and closing live in different systems, and the audit trail spans all of them. What should a CDFI specifically look for in an LOS? Four things beyond the demo: reporting that maps to CDFI Fund requirements like the TLR; flexibility for non-standard borrowers and documents, since your applicants rarely fit conventional templates; a full audit trail on every file for funders and examiners; and pricing that works at community-lender scale, ideally modular so you pay for what you adopt. Will an AI-native LOS replace our loan officers? No. In community lending the decision is the mission, and every platform in this comparison keeps a human in the loop. What changes is where the hours go: away from document chasing, data entry, and memo assembly, toward judgment calls, exceptions, and borrower relationships. The underwriter still signs every memo; the system does the assembly work leading up to it.

title: Korean Mystery Thriller 'Mousetrap' Teaser Trailer and Poster Unveiled Ahead of August 28 Premiere
summary: In an old Korean folktale, when a rat eats someone’s clipped fingernails, they turn into that person. This jarring premise lies behind Netflix’s new mystery thriller series Mousetrap, premiering August 28.
body_text: Entertainment 31 July 2026 Global South Korea Link copied to clipboard In an old Korean folktale, when a rat eats someone’s clipped fingernails, they turn into that person. This jarring premise lies behind Netflix’s new mystery thriller series Mousetrap , premiering August 28. In the newly revealed teaser trailer, audiences are introduced to Moon-jae, a reclusive novelist who uses a pen name and hasn't left home in years, following a solitary daily routine. Then the strange things start: his fingerprint won't unlock his phone, his passwords stop working, and one by one, the things tying him to his own identity slip out of his grasp. Stripped of his money, his name, and any way to prove himself, Moon-jae is plunged into chaos and sets out to hunt down a mysterious figure calling himself "The Rat," who seems to know exactly who Moon-jae is. Directed by Kim Hong-sun ( Dear Hongrang , Money Heist: Korea – Joint Economic Area ), Mousetrap is based on the webtoon “Field Mouse”. Ryu Jun-yeol ( Revelations , The 8 Show ) leads the series as Moon-jae, along with Sul Kyung-gu ( Good News , Kill Boksoon ) as Noja, a fierce loan shark, and Lee Kyoo-hyung ( Prison Playbook , Hi Bye, Mama! ) as Sun-yong, a detective chasing “The Rat.” "Prove I'm real, or I'm the imposter." Mousetrap premieres August 28, only on Netflix. Sungjin Cho PR Manager sungjinc@netflix.com Sally Oh Publicity Specialist sallyoh@netflix.com
